content:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Rudy Giuliani, who was mayor when the September 11, 2001 attacks occurred, were photographed shaking hands at a 25th anniversary memorial ceremony in Lower Manhattan on Friday, despite Giuliani never making a secret of his distaste for New York's first Muslim mayor.

After Mamdani was elected, Giuliani posted on Facebook implying another 9/11 could happen on his watch. He also told Newsmax on Sunday that Mamdani should stay away from Friday's memorial ceremony.

Giuliani told the outlet: "There is no question that he should [skip the memorial]," "I mean, it's for the families and for the country to remember, historically."

Giuliani added: "I lost some friends there, I'm very close to a lot of the victims' families, and I find it offensive that he shows up."

Despite this, the following video shows Mamdani extending the olive branch to Giuliani. Giuliani initially cracked a small smile but appeared to look displeased seconds into the conversation before the two separated.

Mamdani said: "He walked over, we both extended our hands, we said hello to each other. I think what we should all be most focused on are the families, those who responded and are here to hear every single name that was taken 25 years ago and how their families have been strong in the years since."

The Hill noted that Giuliani's reasoning for asking Mamdani to skip the ceremony "related to Mamdani's faith."

Giuliani claimed: "They want to take over us. This is not a case of, 'They just want to be one of the many religions.' They want to dominate us. Mamdani is clearly a proponent of that idea."

The New York Times reported that Mamdani accused multiple former city leaders at a City Hall press conference Tuesday of concealing the truth about air quality near the World Trade Center site after 9/11 from New York City residents.

Mamdani said: "People got sick because the leaders they trusted lied to them and told them it was safe to breathe in toxic air." He added that the number of people who have died from related health issues has surpassed the death toll from the 2001 attacks themselves.
